newsitem.title: USA: CBOT says clearing firm must deliver soybeans.
newsitem.headline: CBOT says clearing firm must deliver soybeans.

text.p: The Chicago Board of Trade said a clearing firm that inadvertently posted 1.16 million bushels of soybeans for delivery against the May contract on Tuesday must complete the delivery.
"A clearing firm inadvertently over-tendered 1,155,000 bushels of May 1997 soybeans for delivery on May 7, 1997," the CBOT Clearing Corporation said in a statement.
"The clearing firm that made this error will complete the delivery of 1,155,000 bushels of soybeans in compliance with the rules and regulations of the CBOT," it said.
A spokesman for the clearing firm, Iowa Grain, was not available for comment.

CBOT did not name the firm that delivered the soybeans in error, but CBOT delivery notices showed Iowa Grain tendered to deliver 1,160,000 bushels of soybeans. Total deliveries posted for May 7 this morning were 1,245,000 bushels.

CBOT floor sources called the mistake a clerical error, saying a number was mistakenly entered into the wrong column, leading the firm to post 1,160,000 bushels of grade one soybeans for delivery instead of 5,000 bushels.

The primary stoppers of the deliveries included Paine Webber with 450,000 bushels, Rand Financial with 375,000 bushels and Dean Witter with 140,000 bushels, according to CBOT issues and stops data released on Tuesday morning.
